pr.title: gh-142560: bytearray: prevent UAF in search-like methods by exporting self buffer
pr.body:
bytearray: prevent UAF in search-like methods by exporting self buffer

Fix a heap use-after-free when bytearray search helpers captured the raw
buffer pointer before normalizing the “sub” argument. A crafted index
or buffer provider could clear/resize the same bytearray during argument
conversion, invalidating the saved pointer and leading to UAF.

Change:
•  For bytearray methods find/rfind/index/rindex/count/startswith/endswith/
  contains/split/rsplit, export a temporary Py_buffer on self and pass
  view.buf/view.len to the Py_bytes* helpers, then release it. While the
  export is live, resizing/clearing raises BufferError, preventing stale
  pointer dereferences.

Tests:
•  Add re-entrancy tests to Lib/test/test_bytes.py that verify BufferError is
  raised when index clears the target during find/count/index/rfind/rindex.

This mirrors existing protection used in bytearray.join and removes the
re-entrancy hazard without changing public APIs.

+    def test_search_methods_reentrancy_raises_buffererror(self):
+        # gh-142560: Raise BufferError if buffer mutates during search arg conversion.
+        class Evil:
+            def __init__(self, ba):
+                self.ba = ba
+            def __buffer__(self, flags):
+                self.ba.clear()
+                return memoryview(self.ba)
+            def __release_buffer__(self, view: memoryview) -> None:
+                view.release()
+            def __index__(self):
+                self.ba.clear()
+                return ord("A")
+
+        def make_case():
+            ba = bytearray(b"A")
+            return ba, Evil(ba)
+
+        for name in ("find", "count", "index", "rindex", "rfind"):
+            ba, evil = make_case()
+            with self.subTest(name):
+                with self.assertRaises(BufferError):
+                    getattr(ba, name)(evil)
+
+        ba, evil = make_case()
+        with self.assertRaises(BufferError):
+            evil in ba
+        with self.assertRaises(BufferError):
+            ba.split(evil)
+        with self.assertRaises(BufferError):
+            ba.rsplit(evil)
+

review_comments.body:
Why does the `BufferError` become possible here?

In my head this part of `test_free_threading_bytearray` mixes full-object assignment and full-object clearing, both of which lock the bytearray being modified (and so serialize the changes / there shouldn't be other exports simultaneously).

I think this critical section is still needed; `ob_exports` which gets incremented when exporting the buffer prevents resizing the array but does not prevent changing the contents; the critical section here guarantees during the sequence contains (https://docs.python.org/3/c-api/typeobj.html#c.PySequenceMethods.sq_contains) the bytearray isn't modified by other python calls.

review_comments.body: Should include in the changelog the changes to `split` and `rsplit`

All the methods that use this helper have `@critical_section` in their Argument Clinic input which means that argument clinic outputs locks for self. That means this critical section locking is redundant (it's all inside a critical section already). Ex:

 https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/d844d22cb00e4a8a224a79109870ae13caddeaef/Objects/clinic/bytearrayobject.c.h#L153-L155

Should be able to change to `_Py_CRITICAL_SECTION_ASSERT_OBJECT_LOCKED(self);` which will validate that the critical section is held without needing to begin/end a new critical section here.

review_comments.body:
The code is touched in the PR (https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/142564/changes#diff-6878f29bbfb711dc7cd2a89b2b2941b1f900b6367d30181a2ff45460b591b04cL1890 / line 1909 is the implementation `byearray_rsplit_impl`). 

While buffer protocol on bytearray _should_ return the same values as `PyByteArray_AS_STRING` and `PyByteArray_GET_SIZE` that isn't guaranteed. A `bytearray` subclass can override the buffer protocol implementation and before this change that wouldn't matter (`.rsplit` didn't use the buffer protocol), while after it will get called which is a user-visible change. Not something I think happens often, but want to capture all the changes in the change log so if someone does have unexpected behavior inside `byearray.rsplit` come up in an upgrade they have a trail of breadcrumbs back to here which makes resolving a lot easier.
